newsitem.title: USA: Kmart expects Q4 charge on Mexico sale.
newsitem.headline: Kmart expects Q4 charge on Mexico sale.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Friday it plans to record a small charge against its fourth quarter earnings due to the sale of its 50 percent interest in Kmart Mexico SA de CV.

Kmart investor relations director Robert Burton said the charge "should not materially affect" Kmart's earnings and added that he did not know whether the retailer would specify the charge in its earnings report in the fourth quarter, expected to be reported in early March.

Kmart said late Thursday that it and Mexican partner El Puerto de Liverpool SA de CV each agreed to sell their 50 percent interests in Kmart Mexico to the country's second-largest retail group, Controladora Comercial Mexicana SA, for a total of $148.5 million in cash.
Kmart plans to use its cash proceeds of $74.25 million to repay indebtedness, Burton said.
He added that the four Mexican hypermarket stores operated by Kmart Mexico were "slightly unprofitable" in the fiscal 1996 year-to-date period.
Kmart Mexico has three stores in Mexico City and one in Cuernavaca and is opening a fifth store this spring in Puebla.
